title: Personal operating contract + weekly sprintboard — Arpita
content:
Context / intent:
This is my lightweight personal operating contract for the next two quarters plus an attached weekly sprintboard I keep in my head. The goal is to be explicit about tradeoffs I commit to (time, upskilling, visibility) and to preserve a concise evidence trail for calibration conversations. Not polished — deliberately terse.

Top-level commitments (contract):
- 2x deep-focus blocks (90m) on Tuesdays and Thursdays — defensible, calendar-locked
- One calibration-ready summary every biweekly 1:1 (2 slides, 3 bullets each): impact, risk, ask
- Maintain a rolling 6-week experiment list (max 3 active experiments)
- Reserve Friday afternoon for synthesis, backlog grooming, and async prep

How I measure adherence (signal):
- Calendar match rate: target >= 80% deep-block completion per month
- Evidence snippets captured: at least one concrete metric or quote per major initiative per sprint
- Visibility metric: 2 cross-team updates per month (email or Miro)

Behavioral anchors (what I do when stretched):
- Default to clarifying question in Slack before assuming scope creep
- When asked to escalate, state 1) why now, 2) desired outcome, 3) ask of person receiving the escalation
- If I miss a deep-focus block, mark a recovery slot same week or accept the slip and note cause

Weekly sprintboard (template I actually use) — copy/paste into every Monday note:
- Week dates: <Mon — Sun>
- Top 3 priorities (outcomes, not tasks):
  1) [Outcome] e.g., "Draft Dedicated onboarding checklist v0.3 — ready for field testing"
  2) [Outcome]
  3) [Outcome]
- Triage / blockers (explicit asks to remove blockers):
  - Blocker A -> owner (Jonah) -> needed by Thu
  - Blocker B -> owner (infra) -> escalate?
- Evidence to capture this week:
  - Metric: average onboarding time (baseline 8d) — target -20%
  - Customer quote / CS note to drop into calibration slide
- Quick wins (3): small things I can finish in <2h
- Learning/skill micro-goal: 30m on SQL perf patterns or read one kernel optimization note

Biweekly 1:1 summary (how I structure the 2-slide update):
- Slide 1: What I shipped / measurable impact (3 bullets)
- Slide 2: Risks, open choices, and specific asks (person + concrete ask + timeline)
- One behavioral note for manager: where I want feedback (e.g., delegation efficiency, clarity on priorities)

6-week experiment roster (rolling):
- [Exp-1] Reduce tokenization cost by introducing per-route cache TTLs (owner: me). Hypothesis: 8–12% cost reduction for small prompts. Success metric: >=6% cost down after 4 weeks. Status: active.
- [Exp-2] Run templated onboarding email A/B (owner: CS). Hypothesis: clearer docs => fewer follow-ups. Success: response rate up or support tickets down. Status: paused.
- [Exp-3] Micro-workshop on "asserting scope" for hiring managers (owner: People Ops). Status: planning.

Notes to self (scratch/fragments — unfiltered):
- Keep calibration examples short — managers like 1x metric + 1x quote
- Avoid rehashing design history in 1:1 unless asked
- When writing ask: always include what NOT to do if we get partial approval
- "Evidence snippet" example: "Reduced median onboarding latency from 78h -> 60h (23%), measured across 12 pilot orgs; anecdotal CS note: 'much smoother'"

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Do I keep two deep-focus blocks indefinitely or switch to a single larger block + small daily triage? (Test in Q2)
- Which experiment is highest ROI? Need a short scoring rubric (effort x impact x risk)

Immediate actions (this morning):
- Draft 1:1 slide pack (first pass) — 45m
- Ping Jonah for blocker matrix update — 10m
- Add onboarding metric hooks to dashboard (SQL snippet) — 30m

Useful templates & snippets I reuse:
- "Ask" template: "I need X by DATE to achieve Y. If not possible, fallback is Z. Who can help: [names]."
- Calibration slide header: (1) KPI, (2) baseline, (3) current status, (4) action/ask

Quick archive log (evidence I keep for calibration):
- 2025-10-05: onboarding pilot — median time 78h (pilot=12 orgs)
- 2025-11-19: cache experiment kickoff — initial perf numbers collected
- 2026-01-12: CS quote from Beta org A — 'onboarding feels lighter'

Meta-reflection (monthly, 15m ritual):
- What small change produced outsized effect last month?
- Where did I spend cognitive load that could be systematized?
- One thing to stop doing next month

Endnote: keep this lightweight — the goal is better clarity, lower friction. Revisit contract every quarter or when a role-change happens.
